thread:
alex: Hey team — seeing a couple OOMs on model-x when serving 8k tokens on dedicated-2. Not reproducible locally. Can someone generate a heap map / allocator snapshot from a live worker? Need something like jemalloc stats or a heaptrack dump so we can check fragmentation vs leak.

rachel: I can grab jemalloc stats. Which host / PID? Is this on dedicated-2/gpu-03?

alex: Yes, gpu-03. PID should be the runtime process (redwood-runtime). I saw OOM kills around 11:12 UTC. If you can run the `je-metrics` script from infra it prints useful stats.

rachel: On it. Quick note — if we attach profilers in prod plz use sampling only (no full alloc hooks) and keep runtime restart window small.

devon: tagging in case SRE needs to adjust cgroup OOM settings. @sre-bot any constraints on running `heaptrack` on a live node?

sre-bot: heaptrack on prod is allowed for short runs (<2m) during low traffic by request. Please open an incident ticket with run timeframe. Automatic alert if CPU > 85%.

ben: If fragmentation, we might see large unused arenas in jemalloc. Look for `arenas: n` and `active` vs `mapped` bytes. Also check `small` vs `large` stats.

rachel: I ran `malloc_conf` query and current config: `lg_dirty_mult:1, narenas:64, decay_ms:15000`. Dumping jemalloc stats now:```
--- jemalloc stats (excerpt) ---
allocated: 11.9G
active:    24.1G
mapped:    30.5G
retained:  7.8G
--- end ---
```

alex: Hmm active >> allocated suggests fragmentation. Which makes sense with long-lived KV cache + spikes. Can we get per-arena fragmentation?

ben: `jeprof` + `je_malloc_stats_print` with `JEMALLOC_PER_ARENA:true` will help. Alternatively run `je-heapmap` (one-liner) to produce per-arena heatmap.

rachel: started `je-heapmap --pid 4321 --duration 60 --out /tmp/heapmap-gpu03.json` (PID confirmed). Will upload to shared drive when done.

devon: Alex, can you link the PR that added the large prefix cache? I'm wondering if growth strategy is contributing.
alex: PR #849 — it switched cache weight to max(8MB, tokens*avg_token_bytes). Might be aggressive.

ben: Possible quick mitigation: reduce cache cap to 4MB and enable purging of arenas after idle window. But test impact on latency.

rachel: Upload complete: https://drive.redwood/heapmaps/gpu03/1764123456-heapmap-gpu03.json

ben: I pulled it — heatmap shows 40% of arenas with >50% fragmentation in 128-512B bins. Likely internal fragmentation from small-object growth + arena affinity.

devon: Suggest two steps: (1) change `narenas` to auto detect based on CPU cores (current fixed 64 might be too high), (2) enable `purge: true`/shrink policy for arenas after 30s idle. I'll open a small config PR.

alex: Can you also add a benchmark invocation to the CI perf job to run a 8k token gen for 5 iterations so we detect regressions? Might help catch this in the future.

devon: Yep — adding a `perf/oom-smoke` that runs under the same `malloc_conf`. Will tag you on the PR.

rachel: One more datapoint: `pmap` shows RSS 27G while process reports 12G used. So kernel-level mapping hasn't been returned. Might need `mallctl`-triggered purging.

ben: If arenas are the issue, `mallctl(`
